3.4.1.5-r1.burton_quote: worship by all means the Gods of the place

3.4.1.5-r2.burton_quote: Because God is immense and infinite, and his nature cannot perfectly be known, it is convenient he should be as diversely worshipped, as every man shall perceive or understand

3.4.1.5-r3.burton_quote: that all those should participate of eternal happiness, who lived an holy and innocent life, what religion soever they professed

3.4.1.5-r4.burton_quote: that he put all Heretics to silence

3.4.1.5-r5.burton_quote: club-law, fire and sword for Heretics, compel them, stop their mouths not with disputations

3.4.1.5-r6.burton_quote: speaks of a fellow that in like case complained to him, and desired his help: I asked him (saith he) what the matter was, he replied, I am continually meditating of heaven and hell, and methinks I see and talk with fiery spirits, smell brimstone, &c., and am so carried away with these conceits, that I can neither eat, nor sleep, nor go about my business: I cured him (saith Rhasis) partly by persuasion, partly by Physic, and so have I done by many others
